'''Jeffrey Goldstone''' (3 September 1933 – 12 October 2026) was a British [[theoretical physicist]] and academic who was an emeritus physics faculty member at the [[MIT]] [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]]. Goldstone worked at the [[University of Cambridge]] until 1977. 

He is noted for his work on the mathematical formalism of [[quantum field theory]] and his contributions to [[quantum optimization algorithms]]. The [[Goldstone boson]] and the related Goldstone theorem are named after him. 

==Life and career==
Born in Manchester, England, on 3 September 1933, Goldstone was educated at [[Manchester Grammar School]] and [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] (B.A. 1954, Ph.D. 1958). He worked on the theory of [[nuclear matter]] under the guidance of [[Hans Bethe]] and developed modifications of [[Feynman diagrams]] for non-relativistic many-fermion systems, which are currently referred to as Goldstone diagrams.<ref name="Atomic Many-Body Theory">{{cite book | author=Lindgren I. & Morrison J. | title=Atomic Many-Body Theory | edition=2nd | page=215 | publisher=Springer-Verlag | year=1986 | isbn=0-387-10504-2}}</ref> In 1957, he proved the [[linked-cluster theorem]], showing that only connected diagrams contribute to the calculation.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Fetter |first1=Alexander L. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0wekf1s83b0C |title=Quantum Theory of Many-particle Systems |last2=Walecka |first2=John Dirk |date=2003-06-20 |publisher=Courier Corporation |isbn=978-0-486-42827-7 |language=en}}</ref>

Goldstone was a research fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], from 1956 to 1960 and held visiting research posts at [[Copenhagen]], [[CERN]] and Harvard. During this time, his research focus shifted to [[particle physics]] and he investigated the nature of [[Relativistic field theory|relativistic field theories]] with spontaneously broken symmetries. With [[Abdus Salam]] and [[Steven Weinberg]], he proved that in such theories zero-mass particles (Nambu–Goldstone bosons) must exist.

From 1962 to 1976, Goldstone was a faculty member at Cambridge. In the early 1970s, with [[Peter Goddard (physicist)|Peter Goddard]], [[Claudio Rebbi]] and [[Charles Thorn]], he worked out the light-cone quantization theory of relativistic strings. He moved to the [[United States|USA]] in 1977 as Professor of Physics at [[MIT]], where he was appointed the Cecil and Ida Green Professor of Physics in 1983 and was director of the MIT Center for Theoretical Physics in 1983–1989.

He published research on solitons in quantum field theory with [[Roman Jackiw]] and [[Frank Wilczek]], and on the quantum strong law of large numbers with [[Edward Farhi]] and [[Samuel Gutmann]]. Since 1997, he has worked, with Farhi, Gutmann, [[Michael Sipser]] and [[Andrew Childs]], on [[quantum computing]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeffrey Goldstone » MIT Physics |url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/jeffrey-goldstone/ |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=MIT Physics |language=en-US}}</ref> Together they introduced [[adiabatic quantum computation]] in 2000 and the [[Quantum optimization algorithms#Quantum approximate optimization algorithm|quantum approximate optimization (QAOA) algorithm]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blekos |first=Kostas |last2=Brand |first2=Dean |last3=Ceschini |first3=Andrea |last4=Chou |first4=Chiao-Hui |last5=Li |first5=Rui-Hao |last6=Pandya |first6=Komal |last7=Summer |first7=Alessandro |date=2024-06-02 |title=A review on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm and its variants |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370157324001078 |journal=Physics Reports |series=A review on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm and its variants |volume=1068 |pages=1–66 |doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2024.03.002 |issn=0370-1573|arxiv=2306.09198 }}</ref>

Goldstone died on 12 October 2026, aged 93.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heatley |first=Kim |date=2026-10-14 |title=Jeffrey Goldstone, pioneering theoretical physicist and MIT professor emeritus, dies at 93 |url=https://physics.mit.edu/news/jeffrey-goldstone-pioneering-theoretical-physicist-and-mit-professor-emeritus-dies-at-93/ |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=MIT Physics |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] (elected 1977),<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2007 |title=List of Fellows of the Royal Society 1660 – 2007 |url=https://people.iith.ac.in/m_vidyasagar/images/royal-society/Fellows1660-2007.pdf |website=The Royal Society}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1977),{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1987).<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Honorary Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] (2000).{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] of the American Physical Society (1981) "For his contribution to nuclear physics, condensed matter physics and to quantum field theory, in establishing the first rigorous diagrammatic technique for the many-body problem and in proving a fundamental theorem on spontaneously broken global symmetry."<ref>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Jeffrey%20Goldstone&year=1981 APS Citation]</ref>
* [[Institute of Physics Michael Faraday Medal and Prize|Guthrie Medal]] of the [[Institute of Physics]] (London) (1983)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Faraday Medal and Prize recipients {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold-medals/michael-faraday-medal-and-prize-recipients |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] of the International Center for Theoretical Physics (Trieste) (1991) shared with [[Stanley Mandelstam]], "for his fundamental clarification of the phenomenon of spontaneous symmetry violation in relativistic quantum field theory."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dirac Medallists 1991 {{!}} ICTP |url=https://www.ictp.it/home/dirac-medallists-1991 |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=www.ictp.it}}</ref>
